ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, D is a point on side $BC$, and $AB=AD=DC$. If $AC=BC$, find the measure of $\angle C$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle C=x$,\\
since $AD=DC$,\\
thus $\angle DAC=\angle C=x$,\\
therefore $\angle ADB=2x$,\\
since $AB=AD$,\\
thus $\angle B=\angle ADB=2x$,\\
since $AC=BC$,\\
thus $\angle BAC=\angle B=2x$,\\
in $\triangle ABC$, $2x+2x+x=180^\circ$,\\
therefore $x=\boxed{36^\circ}$,\\
therefore the degree of $\angle C$ is $\boxed{36^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a triangle ABC, A is above, B and C are at the two ends of the base, and BC is a horizontal base; point D is located on BC and between B and C; a line segment AD is drawn from A to D, and there are also sides AB and AC. The problem gives AB=AD=DC, and AC=BC. Reasoning: Let ∠C=x. Because D is on BC, ∠ACD is the same as ∠C of triangle ABC, namely ∠ACD=x. From AD=DC, triangle ADC is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠DAC=∠ACD=x. Thus in triangle ADC, ∠ADC=180°-2x. Also because DB and DC are opposite rays on the same straight line, ∠ADB is the supplementary angle of ∠ADC, so ∠ADB=180°-(180°-2x)=2x. From AB=AD, triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, so ∠ABD=∠ADB=2x. Because B, D, C are collinear, ∠ABD is ∠ABC, therefore ∠ABC=2x. Also AC=BC, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, so ∠BAC=∠ABC=2x. Finally in triangle ABC, ∠BAC+∠ABC+∠C=180°, namely 2x+2x+x=180°, so 5x=180°, x=36°. Therefore ∠C=36°.
